title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing the previous page). Let Y ⊂ X be closed and T a conic neighbourhood of Y in X. This is a closed neighbourhood T with boundary Ṫ and a 'multiplication' I × Ṫ → T, with I = [0,1]. The map sends {0} × Ṫ onto Y (written 0·Ṫ), identifies T with the mapping cylinder of the map Ṫ → Y, and gives T_λ = λT for λ ∈ ]0,1[.

Sub-conic sets (12). A (closed) subset T' ⊂ T is called sub-conic, or conic in T, if:
(a) T' is stable under the multiplications by λ ∈ I;
(b) with the induced operation, T' is itself a conic neighbourhood. This should be read as a neighbourhood of Y' = T' ∩ Y, not of Y.

NB. Necessarily Ṫ' = T' ∩ Ṫ and T'_λ = T' ∩ T_λ. The datum of T' is equivalent to two pieces of data: a closed subset Ṫ' ⊂ Ṫ, and a closed subset Y' ⊂ Y with Y' ⊃ 0·Ṫ'. Then T' = Im(I × Ṫ' → T) ∪ Y'. So T' is the sub-mapping-cylinder over Ṫ', plus possibly extra points of Y not reached by the cone lines.

Marginal definition. T' is strictly conic if T' ∩ Y = 0·Ṫ'. In that case T' is exactly the cone (mapping cylinder) on a closed subset of Ṫ.

Compatibility. A conic structure on T ⊃ Y is compatible with a family of closed subsets T_i (i ∈ I) if each T_i is conic for that structure. For a conic neighbourhood T of Y in X and a closed X' ⊂ X:
- T is compatible with X' if X' ∩ T is conic in T.
- T is strictly compatible with X' if three things hold. First, T is a strict conic neighbourhood, i.e. the rescaling-by-λ condition of the previous page holds. Second, Ṫ ⊂ X* = X \ T° admits a cylindrical (collar) neighbourhood compatible with X'* = X' ∩ X*. Equivalently, continuing on the next page, there is a neighbourhood E of Ṫ in X* and a homeomorphism E ≅ Ṫ × [0,1], restricting to t ↦ (t,0) on Ṫ, under which X' ∩ E = X'_0 × [0,1] for a closed X'_0 ⊂ Ṫ.

Purpose. This is the local-structure part of a theory of 'déploiement' of stratified spaces. Conic (mapping-cylinder) neighbourhoods of a closed stratum should be compatible with the other closed unions of strata, both inside the tube (conic compatibility) and across its boundary into the complement (collar compatibility). That makes the tube/complement decomposition of a stratified space respect the stratification and allows induction on strata. It is the topological counterpart of Thom–Mather control data, written as mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods with compatible collars.
errors: Condition (12 b) literally asks T' to be a conic neighbourhood 'de Y'. It must be of Y' = T' ∩ Y, otherwise X' ∩ T could never be conic for a proper closed X'. The NB, which introduces Y' ⊃ 0·Ṫ', implicitly corrects this.
Slip: 'strictement compatible avec T' should read 'strictement compatible avec X''.
Closedness of T' is needed for the NB's description (Ṫ', Y' closed). It is only added as an afterthought ('fermés') in the compatibility definition.

In 'compatible', non-strict conic subsets allow Y' to contain points of Y not in 0·Ṫ' (e.g. pieces of X' lying entirely in Y). This is harmless but means compatibility alone does not make X' ∩ T a cone. The strict notion addresses this, and Grothendieck evidently noticed it (marginal addition).

ideas.what: Sub-conic subsets of a conic (mapping-cylinder) neighbourhood, classified by a closed Ṫ' ⊂ Ṫ and a closed Y' ⊂ Y containing 0·Ṫ'.
ideas.modern_name: Sub-mapping-cylinder / stratified conic neighbourhood (cf. Siebenmann CS sets, mapping cylinder neighbourhoods)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Siebenmann (1972), Quinn (1988), Hughes (teardrop neighbourhoods); Thom–Mather in the smooth/Whitney setting
ideas.where_published: Programmatic only: Esquisse d'un programme §5 on 'topologie modérée' and dévissage of stratified spaces

ideas.what: Strictly conic subset: T' ∩ Y = 0·Ṫ', i.e. T' is the cone on a closed subset of the boundary.
ideas.modern_name: Conic/cone-like compatibility of strata with a tubular neighbourhood

ideas.what: Strict compatibility of a conic neighbourhood with a closed subset X': a collar of Ṫ in the complement X \ T° in which X' is a product X'_0 × [0,1].
ideas.modern_name: Stratified collar / compatible collar; transversality of strata to the tube boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brown's collaring theorem (1962); stratified versions by Siebenmann, Quinn, Hughes

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'déploiement' program splits compatibility of a stratum's tube with other strata into two separate conditions. One is a conic condition inside the tube; the other is a collar (cylindrical) condition on the complement side. He notes the cylindrical one is not a special case of the conic one (next page). This is a purely topological, axiomatic packaging of Thom–Mather-style control data. It is only a documentary detail of an unpublished program sketched in the Esquisse; it does not go beyond Siebenmann/Quinn/Hughes.
missed.quote: On dit qu'il est strictement compatible avec T, si T est voisinage cônique strict, et s'il existe un voisinage cylindrique de Ṫ dans X* = X \ T°, compatible avec X'* = X'∩X*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for reconstructing the never-written 'tame topology' dévissage theory of the Esquisse. Mathematically the notions are standard in topological stratification theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful foundational definitions (sub-conic sets, strict compatibility via compatible collars) that are routine relative to Siebenmann/Quinn/Hughes-style stratification theory. Their interest is mainly as documentation of Grothendieck's unpublished déploiement program.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: read 'Soit T un voisi. cônique de Y.' ('fondamental' is doubtful), with the crossed-out 'X ⊃ Y, X …' below.
'Soient T'_ξ ⊂ T': the subscript ξ is an artifact; read 'Soit T' ⊂ T'. The underlined term is 'sous-cônique' / 'cônique dans T'.

NB lines: the inserted text reads approximately 'la donnée de T' équivaut à celle d'un sous-ensemble fermé Ṫ' de Ṫ et d'un sous-ensemble fermé Y' de Y, tel que Y' ⊃ 0.Ṫ', et on a T' = Im(I × Ṫ' → T) ∪ Y''. It is not 'le domaine de T' équivaut' / 'et dit un sous-voisinage cônique'.
Left marginal note (diagonal): 'On dit que T' est cônique strict si T' ∩ Y = 0.Ṫ', i.e. si T' est le cône d'une partie fermée Ṫ' de Ṫ' (approximately).
Condition (12 a): 'stable par les multiplications λ ∈ I'; the crossed-out word at the right is a deleted alternative, not '{λ ≠ 0}'.
Lower left margin: 'Déf. strict' with an arrow, plus a note roughly 'mettre à part la définition des voisinages côniques stricts'.
